notes: Spec asserts two bullets: (1) Session appears in ready within 1s of agent launch and (2) PID bound within 1s. Both phases anchor to recording start (agent launch) and budget 1000ms — claudecode's pre-session row (proc-<PID>) satisfies both, independent of lazy UUID-transcript materialization. Under desktop-local the anchor and the budget still hold (birth measured at +36..71ms across 11 recordings), but the STATE at birth differs: Claude Desktop creates the session by SUBMITTING the prompt, so the row appears already working and reaches ready only when the first turn ends. Grading that as 'ready within 1s' measured first-turn duration instead of birth latency (2.1s-16.5s, scaling with the cell's workload). Hence the desktop-local expected_states override. It lists both states because which one occurs is a daemon-internal race: transcript activity first yields working (10 of 11 recordings), PID discovery first yields a presession row in ready (1 of 11). The recipe's send+wait_turn steps materialize the UUID transcript but the spec does NOT assert anything about it; the transcript bullets live with basic-turn.

text: Session appears in ready within 1s of agent launch
